title: Linkage of cancer registry data with other medical registries
summary:
Germany has a large number of medical registries with different focuses and objectives. In contrast to many other European countries, the case-related linking of data from different registries is not yet common practice in Germany. 

This project aims to compare and link data from three medical registries with data from the clinical cancer registries (CCR) of the individual federal states in a de facto anonymized manner. The participating medical registries are the national registry for patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) (RABBIT), the national registry for patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) (MS registry) and the German cystic fibrosis registry (CF registry). The aim of the project is to successfully link patient data across registers with other data sources.

interventions.name: Patients with Multiple Sclerosis from the German MS-Registry
Patients with cystic fibrosis from the German Cystic Fibrosis Registry
Patients with rheumatoid arthritis from the Rabbit Registry

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
RABBIT: rheumatoid arthritis diagnosis confirmed by a rheumatologist, start of DMARD therapy, age of onset at least 16 years, written consent

MS registry: MS diagnosed according to McDonald criteria, place of residence in Germany, written consent

CF registry: Cystic fibrosis (according to AWMF guideline 026/023 Diagnosis of cystic fibrosis from June 2013), CFSPID (CF screening positive, inconclusive diagnosis) (according to Munck, J Cyst Fibros 2015), CFTR-associated disease (according to AWMF guideline 026/023 Diagnosis of cystic fibrosis from June 2013)
Exclusion criteria:
Medical registry: missing declaration of consent and missing or "unknown" gender entry
